newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-SMITH'S COACH AND EUROPEAN OFFICIALS END DISCORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SMITH'S COACH AND EUROPEAN OFFICIALS END DISCORD.

text.p: The coach and husband of Ireland's triple Olympic champion Michelle Smith has made his peace with European swimming's governing body, a top official said on Sunday.
Harm Beyer, honorary secretary of the European Swimming League (LEN), said Erik de Bruin had made "a kind of apology" for using a false accreditation at the 1995 European championships in Vienna.
"The suspicions we had against him, how he got accredited in Vienna, were confirmed," Beyer said after meeting the Dutchman.
"He admitted he did as we suspected. He stated he thought it was not wrong. There was a kind of apology. The matter's settled."

Beyer said last week an accreditation document containing De Bruin's picture and the personal details of a Belgian team coach had been detected at a doping control in Vienna and the matter would have to be clarified for De Bruin to be accredited in Seville.
The coach is a controversial figure who has just finished a four-year suspension for a positive drugs test during his career as an international athlete.
"I did not insist he fell on his knees," Beyer said. "We agreed he did wrong and he promised not to do it again. That's enough." De Bruin has been accredited for Seville.
Smith, who will compete in Seville under her married name as Michelle de Bruin for the first time at an international championships, has been refused a late entry in the 100 metres butterfly.
Already entered for six events, the triple Olympic champion submitted an extra application to swim the 100 metres butterfly but missed a 10-day deadline.
Beyer said the late entry, which was subsequently included in a provisional official start list, had been dated August 7 and received a day or two later.
The swimming events do not begin until Tuesday (Aug 19) but the championships themselves opened on August 13 with the other aquatic disciplines and that was the relevant date, he added.

Smith, who has made phenomenal progress since De Bruin took charge of her swimming after the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, is down to compete in the 200 metres butterfly, 200 and 400 individual medley and 200, 400 and 800 freestyle.
She won the 200 butterfly and 200 individual medley at the 1995 European championships and prevailed in the 200 and 400 individual medley and 400 freestyle at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.
